ca_west_face_left.blurb: This is the left-hand section of the long west wall of Medlicott Dome, a granite dome in Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite, at roughly 8,900 feet. Ten routes, mostly trad with a pair of bolted lines, and the grades skip the middle: two at 5.9, then four around 5.11 and four around 5.12. Expect face and knob climbing, with several routes running two to four pitches. The wall picks up sun from midday into the evening, and the way down is a walk off over the top of the dome toward the southwest. A good stop for strong trad climbers who like sustained face moves.

ca_roadkill_rock.blurb: A single sandstone boulder, around 30 feet tall, in the Castle Rock area of the Santa Cruz Mountains in the South Bay. It stands right beside the Skyline Trail and can be seen from the road, so there is hardly any walking. Most of the ten problems are easy, from VB-level up to about V2, with traverses and an arete among the favorites. A couple of much harder problems and one short bolted line in the 5.11 range add a little top end. Long slings from a pipe on top make top-roping straightforward, so it also suits a quick stop with a rope.

ca_2_lower_brother.blurb: Lower Brother is a granite formation on the north side of Yosemite Valley, a little under a mile west of Camp 4. Nearly everything here is traditional multi-pitch climbing, from two to eight pitches, with a single sport route. Grades are moderate to stout: one 5.8, four at 5.9, three at 5.10 and two at 5.11. The well-known base routes pick up afternoon shade. The walk from the roadside pullout is short but there is no obvious trail through the trees, so cairns and some route-finding help. The scrambly approach and descent tend to keep the crowds thin.

ca_simian_slab.blurb: Simian Slab is a low-angle slab among the Monkeyface Boulders, off Highway 38 in the San Bernardino Mountains at about 4,600 feet. All ten problems are bouldering, and nearly all of them are very easy: eight at the VB level, then a V0 and a V1. The rock is smooth and good quality, and a couple of steeper problems sit on the back side. It lies just south of and below the Monkey3 Boulder, on the right of the east trail. That makes it a friendly warm-up or a place for beginners. The cooler months are the best time to visit, and rattlesnakes have been seen on the approach in summer.

ca_south_cave_rock.blurb: South Cave Rock is the farther of the two big formations that make up Cave Corridor, in Joshua Tree's Sheep Pass area, a short distance from the Ryan Mountain trailhead lot. The monzogranite is gritty and a bit loose or grainy in places. Ten routes mix trad, aid and one bolted line. Most of the free climbs fall between 5.6 and 5.9, with a few 5.10 and 5.11 lines near the top, and there is one aid route. The corridor has a northeast wall inside and a northwest wall facing the road. It is a quick, low-commitment stop for moderate trad.
ca_south_cave_rock.approach: A short walk from the Ryan Mountain trailhead lot: follow the trail briefly and turn toward the rocks, or head to the cave and circle around to enter the corridor.

ca_west_buttress_2.blurb: A small granite crag at Sugarloaf, above Kyburz on the Highway 50 corridor, sitting just west of the lowest point of the south face at about 4,700 feet. It is reached by a few minutes of walking on a small trail. The face looks south and gets plenty of sun. Layout is two buttresses either side of an obvious groove, plus a slabby face farther left. Ten routes, mostly bolted, some needing a few trad pieces and a few fully trad, running from 5.7 up to a single 5.11. Low-angle, well protected and easy to top-rope, so it works well for a first lead.
